BREAKING: Foreign holdings of US Treasuries jumped +$83 billion in August, to $9.33 trillion, their 6th-highest total on record.

The surge was driven by Canada, which raised its holdings by +$38 billion, to $465 billion, its 4th-highest on record.

This was followed by Belgium, which increased its holdings by +$20 billion, to a record $491 billion.

The UK, the 2nd-largest holder, raised its holdings by +$11 billion, to a record $1.01 trillion.

Meanwhile, Japan, the largest foreign holder, cut its holdings by -$36 billion, to $1.07 trillion, its lowest since November 2024.

China, the 3rd-largest holder, reduced its holdings by -$27 billion, to $591 billion, its lowest level since August 2008.

Foreign holdings of US Treasuries are rising despite continued selling in Japan and China.

BREAKING: US housing starts fell -5.2% MoM in September, to an annualized rate of 1.22 million, the 2nd-lowest reading since May 2020.

This follows MoM declines of -4.9% and -5.9% in July and August.

Single-family housing starts dropped -4.6% MoM last month, to 859,000, the 2nd-lowest since April 2023.

At the same time, multifamily housing starts fell -7.2%, to 349,000, the 2nd-lowest since May 2025.

Higher mortgage rates and worsening affordability are heavily weighing on housing demand.

Furthermore, elevated housing inventories and falling homebuilder confidence are discouraging new construction.

The US housing market is frozen.

posts.name: The Kobeissi Letter
posts.text:
AI-related borrowing is skyrocketing.

US Dollar-denominated AI-related corporate bond issuance is up to $419 billion so far in 2026, the highest annual figure on record.

This represents a +90% YoY increase from full-year 2025 and a +437% increase from full-year 2024.

Year-to-date, Alphabet, $GOOGL, Amazon, $AMZN, Meta, $META, Microsoft, $MSFT, and Oracle, $ORCL, have issued a combined $157 billion in corporate bonds, accounting for 37% of the total.

This is followed by investment-grade and high-yield data center and computing companies, which have raised $66 billion and $37 billion, respectively, and together account for ~25% of AI-related issuance.

Other AI-linked corporate bonds have represented $159 billion, or 38%.

The AI revolution is driving an unprecedented wave of corporate borrowing.

INFLEQTION CEO MATT KINSELLA SAYS THE US GOVERNMENT IS BETTING ON QUANTUM ACROSS THE BOARD

And Infleqtion is involved in all of it

He walked @Sam_Badawi through how three parts of the government are moving at once.

The Department of War is buying quantum sensors and clocks so the military can navigate and keep time without GPS, and it's laying the groundwork to buy quantum computers.

The Department of Commerce had NIST review the entire quantum industry. Kinsella believes it found the industry moving faster than anyone expected, which pushed the government to act. Commerce then picked a handful of companies to back, and Infleqtion signed a letter of intent for a $100 million investment.

The Department of Energy plans to put quantum computers in the national labs. Kinsella says it's the same playbook that put the first GPU clusters there, which helped lead to the AI boom we have today.

Never in history have we witnessed market concentration like this.
